shape_hint: A U-shaped bolt bent from round rod: two parallel straight legs a apart (inside width) joined by a semicircular bend wrapping a pipe, with a metric thread of length b cut on the free end of each leg; overall height h from the top of the bend to the leg ends and outside width e across the legs. Drawn in side view as a U with threaded tips, usually shown with two nuts.
notes: DIN 3570 (Rundstahlbuegel / U-bolt, Form A, thread both legs; nuts and washers separate). Row label = DN of the pipe (DN20 = 3/4 in, DN25 = 1 in, DN32 = 1-1/4 in, DN40 = 1-1/2 in, DN50 = 2 in, DN65 = 2-1/2 in, DN80 = 3 in; fasten.it and boltingspecialist agree on the inch labels). a = inside width between legs, b = thread length, h = height (sources call it h1), e = outside width, d1 = pipe OD range the bolt is meant for (single value when only one OD). Additional sizes whose a, thread, b, h and pipe OD agree in 3 sources but whose e has only 2 sources: DN100 (4in): a=120, M16, b=60, h=171, pipe 108-114.3; DN125 (5in): a=148, M16, b=60, h=191, pipe 133-139.7; DN150 (6in): a=176, M16, b=60, h=217, pipe 159-168.3; DN200 (8in): a=228, M20, b=70, h=283, pipe 216-219.1; DN250 (10in): a=282, M20, b=70, h=334, pipe 267-273. fasten.it prints h1 = 15 for DN65 (typo for 125) and pipe 257 for DN250 (typo for 267) - outvoted. The standard's inch pipe U-bolts (MSS SP-58 Type 24 / ASME B18.31.5) are NOT covered. DIN 3570 itself dates from 1968 (no ISO equivalent); rod diameter d2 is not published.
